questions.question: OP-01/O118 (AX-15, reopen of D171): an SFTP server that reports sizes serves /proc/self/status (size 0 at open, 1417 bytes of content); O1 streams it. D168 stops the stream at the reported size, so it delivers nothing. D171 declares every SFTP store 'unknown: a stream ends where a read meets the end', which would deliver 1417 bytes, and says this deviation admits the normal value, which it does not on bytes delivered. What should the Length at open deviation say, and so what may an SFTP caller assume?

options.label: Widen the deviation (Recommended)
options.description: Deviation reads: 'unknown: a stream ends where a read meets the end, or earlier, at the size the server reports at open where it reports one; the read that meets the end can fail (SFTP)'. It now admits the normal value, as 'weakest last' requires, and D171's 'which the deviation admits' becomes true. An SFTP caller may assume a prefix of the content (D6, NP10) and a failing last read; nothing else changes (D168, D170 stand, static per backend, D82 unchanged). Source: AX-15 (deviations ordered, weakest last), D43, D82, D171.

options.label: Condition on the server
options.description: Use D82: the deviation applies only to 'an SFTP server that reports no sizes'; a server that reports them takes the normal value, and a check runs the deviation row only there. Fails D171's own scenario: one server can report a size for some items and none for others, a property of the item, not of the location, which D171 option (b) already rejected.

options.label: SFTP ignores reported size
options.description: Reverse D168 and D169: SFTP never fixes a length at open, every SFTP stream reads to the end met (D169 option b), NP10 Local-only, the deviation text then exact. Appended bytes may be delivered, the final read contacts the server and can fail, D158's 'starts Exhausted for an empty item' never holds on SFTP. Asked and rejected twice (D168, D169).
